findings.reason: the section can close with a second atomic-write owner standing, so §3 must either name `reckon/project_state.py:_durable_replace` as an owner to migrate or fold into `_store` and list it as a named exception with a reason the census cannot ignore.
findings.text: `_durable_replace` fsyncs the file, renames, then fsyncs the directory, and is reached from five sites (project_state.py:1115, :1827, :2035, :2133, :2344); the plan adds `write_json_atomically` beside the pre-existing envelope writer in `_store.py` and bolts a `fsync_directory` flag onto it instead of reconciling the two owners — the census's stated instrument looks for `write`/`write_text` and cannot see a rename made inside a helper, so §3's done-when ("one implementation per concept") reports success while a parallel atomic-write mechanism stays live in the state layer

findings.reason: §1's inventory of "four byte-identical numeric decoders" and §3's "replacing the four identical bodies" undercount the population by at least three, and when the bodies differ only in `float(value)` versus returning the original int, the census's byte-identical grouping floor cannot see them, so §3's one-implementation-per-concept measure is unfalsifiable as written and the plan must state an instrument that can count near-duplicates.
findings.text: the same file that is the numeric decoders' new home (`reckon/_observations.py`, created by commit `c24a4e3cf`) did not migrate five live decoders with the same bool-rejecting body: reckon/crew/lane_document.py:156, reckon/crew/lane_evidence.py:37, reckon/crew/picker/lane_context.py:67, reckon/crew/picker/outcomes.py:39 and reckon/crew/run_time_profile.py:79 all still implement `_number` (bool refused, int/float coerced), and two more near-variants (reckon/schedule.py:29 `_as_number`, reckon/crew/rollout.py:184 `_number`) survive under other names

findings.reason: the plan must either route ledger and promotion through the shared home without a wrapper or, as it does for retained timestamp readers, name the delegate an accepted exception with the circular-import reason so the census figure and the section's claim agree.
findings.text: `_run_streams` is a one-statement delegate to `metering.run_streams`, and promotion.py:3421 is the same, retained only because a module-level import of `metering` from `reckon.crew` is circular (the facade sets its submodule `__path__` after it imports `ledger`); the plan's §3 design says the copies are replaced and never states the exception, so its own done-when undercounts

findings.reason: the section is designed around per-caller flags, so the deep-module goal is not reachable by adding callers; the plan should fix a small default policy and route through the owner, or the writer is a policy-configuration surface rather than a deep module.
findings.text: the plan's design states the writer takes "an `fsync` parameter that defaults on and that each of the 14 callers sets to match what it does today", and the landed signature is `write_json_atomically(path, payload, *, fsync, indent, sort_keys, mode, fsync_directory, create_parents, ensure_ascii)` (reckon/_store.py:463) — seven keyword flags whose values exist so each migrating caller reproduces policy it held before, so the interface is nearly as large as the behaviour it hides and every new caller re-derives a flag combination

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — reckon/_store.py:463 `write_json_atomically` hides one behaviour (write JSON atomically via a sibling rename) behind a seven-keyword interface whose keywords exist only to reproduce each caller's prior serialisation policy.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan's "one atomic JSON writer" leaves reckon/project_state.py:165 `_durable_replace` as a second, older atomic-replace owner with five call sites, and its census cannot see it.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan searched and cites its search rather than assuming prior art: it runs the crew-pattern-review code-depth census (docs/research/data/crew-pattern-review/code-depth/census.py with its pinned snapshots.json) and names the mechanism it extends ("beside the existing envelope writer in reckon/_store.py"), so the reuse map exists and is the plan's own.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — the plan says metering.run_streams "replaces the copies in promotion and the ledger", but the landing retains two function-local delegates and the plan never states why the tool-id machinery cannot be reached directly, leaving its own §3 measure counting three stream enumerations where it claims one per concept.
